The effects of the coronavirus will weigh on economic activity in the near term and pose risks to the economic outlook; however, consistent with the credit channel literature, the Fed’s move to the effective lower bound alongside large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS and expanded repo, discount window, and dollar swap lines should ease external finance premia and help sustain spending and investment (Bernanke–Gertler; Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein; Gertler and Gilchrist). Even in liquidity-trap conditions where policy rates are constrained, balance-sheet tools and lender-of-last-resort facilities can stabilize market functioning and the flow of credit (Eichenbaum–Fuerst; FRBNY market operations). With market- and survey-based inflation expectations anchored by credible inflation-targeting, muted inflation pressures give room to prioritize maximum employment (Svensson; Walsh). Overall, the near-term tone remains negative but is partially offset by the policy response, which reduces downside tail risks.
